content: When establishing glycemic targets for patients, healthcare providers must take into account several critical factors. These include the duration of the patient’s diabetes, their overall life expectancy, the presence and severity of any significant complications, and the patient’s level of motivation and ability to adhere to treatment plans. For individuals who are at an elevated risk of cardiovascular or renal complications, the use of specific pharmacological agents may be advantageous. Medications such as sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors or glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists have demonstrated potential benefits in reducing these risks and should be considered as part of the therapeutic strategy.
